summary: Missoula County crow's nest built 1935 and abandoned 1941 per firelookout.com; sources disagree on its distance from Missoula, and nothing describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1941 per firelookout.com; no source we read describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Crow's nest, per firelookout.com; the 1935 newspaper describes a new station
George Foley sent to the new station in August 1935 to patrol the region (The Missoulian, quoted on Forest Lookouts)

evidence.supports: site in the Lolo National Forest, Missoula County
Forest Service preparing a strategic point for the fire hazard season
evidence.quote: Forest Service officials are making preparations for occupying strategic point during the great fire hazard season

evidence.supports: George Foley sent to the new station, 16 miles north of Missoula
evidence.quote: Saturday George Foley was sent to the new Mosquito peak lookout station in the Rattlesnake valley, 16 miles north of here

evidence.supports: George Foley to patrol between Mosquito Peak and Mount Stuart
evidence.quote: patrol the region between Mosquito Peak and Mount Stuart
A tempoary lookout has been installed there.

evidence.supports: Montana list marks the site as a crow's nest that is abandoned

corrections.why: Both pages say abandoned (firelookout.com gives 1941); neither says the structure is gone

notes_for_editor: Distance conflicts: 12 miles north of Missoula (firelookout.com) vs 16 miles north of Missoula (The Missoulian, 1935, quoted on Forest Lookouts); both kept in the story. The 1941 abandonment rests on firelookout.com alone. The record kind is platform; firelookout.com and the FFLA list say crow's nest, which may be the same kind. Search found no page on Mosquito Peak and no photo. The FFLA list has another Mosquito Peak in Sanders County (Camp, Abandoned); it is a different site and was not used. The Ron Kemnow credit does not appear on the Forest Lookouts page, so it was dropped from the sources.
